comment: Format comparison, 30s of real webcam footage (corpus-real/cam720.mkv) at 320x240@24. All rows re-measured 2026-09-16 on spec v3.8; every SSIM is 'All' computed in the RGBA domain against the identical decoded source frames, so rows are directly comparable. x264=libx264 preset veryfast, AV1=libsvtav1 preset 10, both fed yuv420p. QOV measured with bench_stream.c (range coder on) + the RGBA-domain ssim filter. QOV decode is single-threaded C incl. per-frame SHA-256; ffmpeg decode is multithreaded with asm. See BENCHMARKS.md for the readable summary and repro recipe.

qov_q60_demo_settings.note: range-coded (spec v3.8). LZ4-era: 557.0 kbps, ssim 0.808, decode 315 fps

x264_crf40.note: nearest x264 point to QOV q60 - the matched-quality comparison row

opus_16k_mono_typical.note: libopus voip typical; analytic, not measured (no speech fixture)

verdict: At nearly matched SSIM (x264 crf40 0.833 vs QOV q60 0.809), x264 needs 8.1 kbps where QOV needs 453.5 (~55x). At SSIM ~0.95, x264 is 34.3 kbps and AV1 28.1. QOV buys simplicity (single-header, 3 bit-exact implementations), determinism and license freedom at a large compression cost; decode is ~10x realtime single-threaded at 320x240 including hashing.
